kangaroo-at-2022-felix-01.title: Ignore the rest
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-01.body:
Look only at the shapes with three corners and skip the circles and squares. Box (B) has 4 of them, more than any other box.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-02.title: Compare the two lines
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-02.body:
The second line has the same sandwich and juice as the first line plus **one more juice**. It costs $14 - 12 = 2$ Euros more, so one juice costs 2 Euros.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-02.title: Check
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-02.body:
Juice 2 Euros, sandwich $12 - 2 = 10$ Euros. Sandwich and two juices: $10 + 2 + 2 = 14$ ✓

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-03.title: One left half, one right half
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-03.body:
Anna has exactly one left half and one right half. She may move and turn the pieces, but she cannot get a second copy.

- (A) shows two left halves, (D) shows two equal pieces: impossible.
- In (B) and (C) one piece is a mirror image of a half, which cannot be made by turning.
- In (E) the left piece is the left half, and the right piece is the right half turned upside down. ✓

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-03.title: Turn the right half
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-03.body:
Turn the right half of the mushroom upside down: the cap is now at the bottom with its round end on the left, the stem is at the top, and the straight cut is on the right. That is exactly the right piece in (E).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-04.title: Find the row and the column
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-04.body:
- Rows from the top: 2 coins, 2 coins, **1 coin**, 2 coins. So the new coin goes in the third row.
- Columns from the left: 2 coins, 2 coins, **1 coin**, 2 coins. So the new coin goes in the third column.

The square in the third row and third column is D.

**Answer: (D) square D**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-04.title: Check the letters
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-04.body:
A, C (second row) and B, E would each make a row or a column with 3 coins. Only D is in a row and a column that both have just one coin.

**Answer: (D) square D**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-05.title: Follow the red path
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-05.body:
On the map the red dashed treasure path runs towards the torn corner, but the treasure (the X) is missing. The torn piece must continue the dashed path and the coastline and end with the X.

Only piece (B) has the end of the red path with the X, and its straight paper edges make the missing corner of the map.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-05.title: Rule out the others
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-05.body:
Pieces (A), (C), (D) and (E) show things that are still on the map — the ships, the fish skeleton, the mountains and the people, the skull — so they were not torn off.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-06.title: Compare the heads
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-06.body:
All animals are built from triangles, squares and parallelograms (slanted pieces). The head of the animal in (D) is a long rectangle, twice as long as it is wide. No other animal has such a rectangle.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-06.title: Tick off the shapes
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-06.body:
Triangles are used everywhere. A square appears in (A), (B), (C) and (E). A parallelogram appears in (A), (B), (D) and (E). The long rectangle appears only in (D).

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-07.title: Pair the baskets
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-07.body:
- Baskets 2 and 4 have the same dotted pattern and the same shape: koala and fox.
- Baskets 1 and 3 have the same woven blue-orange pattern (but different shapes): kangaroo and rabbit.

The only basket left is basket 5 for the mouse.

**Answer: (E) Basket 5**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-07.title: Basket 5 is different
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-07.body:
Basket 5 has a light pattern that no other basket has, so it cannot be one of the two pairs. The mouse is the only animal without a partner.

**Answer: (E) Basket 5**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-08.title: Count the neighbours
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-08.body:
On the left 3 blocks lie on top of each other. On the right 2 blocks stand upright, one behind the other, and both touch all three lying blocks.

- Top lying block: the middle block and the 2 standing blocks = 3.
- Middle lying block: top, bottom and the 2 standing blocks = 4.
- Bottom lying block: the middle block and the 2 standing blocks = 3.
- Each standing block: the 3 lying blocks and the other standing block = 4.

Exactly 3 neighbours: the top and the bottom lying blocks.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-08.title: Think of the middle
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-08.body:
The middle block of the stack has one more neighbour than the top and bottom blocks. The standing blocks touch each other and all three lying ones. So only the top and bottom blocks have exactly 3 neighbours.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-09.title: Walk each path
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-09.body:
The kangaroo needs 7 jumps to the right and 4 jumps up.

- (A): after 2 jumps right it jumps up 4 times and lands in the top-left lake. ✗
- (B): after 2 right, 2 up it goes right along the middle row and lands in the lake on the right. ✗
- (C): 2 right, 2 up, 2 right, 2 up, 3 right — it passes between all the lakes and reaches the koala. ✓
- (D): it has arrows to the left at the end and does not reach the koala. ✗
- (E): 2 right, 3 up lands in the top-left lake. ✗

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-09.title: Count the arrows first
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-09.body:
Only paths with 7 right arrows and 4 up arrows reach the koala; (D) does not. Of the others, only (C) avoids the water when you trace it on the grid.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-10.title: Read the shapes
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-10.body:
The shapes are heart, diamond, diamond, club, spade. So the 2nd and 3rd digits are the same, and all other digits are different from each other.

- 34426: 3, 4, 4, 2, 6 ✓
- 34526: 2nd and 3rd digits differ. ✗
- 34423: the 3 appears twice under different shapes. ✗
- 34424: the 4 appears three times. ✗
- 32446: 2nd and 3rd digits differ. ✗

**Answer: (A) 34426**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-10.title: Pattern
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-10.body:
The number must look like ☐ X X ☐ ☐ with four different digits. Only 34426 has this pattern.

**Answer: (A) 34426**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-11.title: Count little squares
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-11.body:
Each stone covers 2 little squares. The path around a square of side 5 fills a $7 \times 7$ square without the $5 \times 5$ middle:

$49 - 25 = 24$ little squares, so $24 \div 2 = 12$ stones.

**Answer: (C) 12**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-11.title: Find the pattern
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-11.body:
Side 1: 4 stones. Side 3: 8 stones. Each time the side grows by 2, every one of the 4 sides gets one more stone, so 4 more stones. Side 5: $8 + 4 = 12$ stones.

**Answer: (C) 12**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-12.title: Count small triangles
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-12.body:
The dots make a grid of small triangles. If all dots were used, each piece would be a big shape of 10 small triangles. Count how many small triangles are missing:

- (A): 3 missing (two notches at the top and the corner at the top right) → 7.
- (B), (C), (D) and (E): 2 missing each → 8.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-12.title: Look at the cut-outs
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-12.body:
Pieces (B), (C), (D) and (E) each have two small triangles cut away. Piece (A) has three small triangles cut away (two pointed notches at the top and the corner at the top right), so it has the least grass.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-13.title: The two shared circles
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-13.body:
The two empty circles in the middle belong to both houses.

Left house: $6 + 2 + 5 = 13$, so the two middle circles add up to $20 - 13 = 7$.

Right house: $3 + 1 + 7 = 11$, so the question mark is $20 - 11 = 9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-13.title: Compare the houses
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-13.body:
Both houses share the middle circles, so the other numbers must have the same sum: $6 + 2 + 5 = 13$ and $3 + 1 + ? = 13$. So $? = 9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-14.title: A good path
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-14.body:
All 8 rooms add up to $1 + 2 + \dots + 8 = 36$. Dino starts in room 1 and ends in room 8.

The path 1 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 3 → 4 → 8 skips only room 2:

$1 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 3 + 4 + 8 = 34$

**Answer: (D) 34**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-14.title: Why not all rooms?
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-14.body:
Colour the rooms like a chessboard: 1, 3, 6, 8 black and 2, 4, 5, 7 white. Each step goes from black to white or back. Dino starts and ends on black, so he always visits one more black room than white rooms. With 4 black rooms he can visit at most 3 white rooms: he must skip a white room. The smallest white room is 2, so the best is $36 - 2 = 34$.

**Answer: (D) 34**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-15.title: Find all three
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-15.body:
- Runa: 15
- Zara: $15 + 3 = 18$
- Biba: Runa has 5 fewer than Biba, so Biba has $15 + 5 = 20$.

The winner is Biba with 20 stripes.

**Answer: (C) 20**

kangaroo-at-2022-felix-15.title: Compare with Runa
kangaroo-at-2022-felix-15.body:
Zara has 3 more than Runa and Biba has 5 more than Runa, so Biba has the most: $15 + 5 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**
